term: per accidens (accidentally) ordered series of causes
definition: A multiplication of causes in which a cause acts in its own right and its having been caused by a predecessor is accidental to its present causing: a craftsman successively uses different hammers, or a man generates as man rather than as son of his father. The source reading that an infinite series of this kind is not impossible is retained in STMT-INFINITE-REGRESS-IMPOSSIBLE-ONLY-IN-PER-SE-SERIES. Its retained legacy two-Prop Lean code is an opaque transcription, not a model of history or a proof of metaphysical possibility. Analyst sibling STMT-PER-SE-HISTORICAL-SERIES-DISTINCTION types a more limited claim: a distinct historical-predecessor relation can have an injective infinite chain while essential dependence on the same members is well-founded and nonempty. No first historical member is assumed. This witnesses formal compatibility only, not that all per-accidens series are possible, that an actual infinite past exists, or that the relations satisfy the source intended causal meaning.
